Reynolds family tobacco fortune, has filed a $9 million libel suit against the Washington Star for an article it published on the Bagleys March 19. Vicki Bagley charges in the suit that the Star’s article, “Incongruities Mark Lives of Socialite Bagleys,’’ was published with malicious intent. A few days before the article appeared, Bagley was indicted for fraud and conspiracy in connection with alleged price manipulations of Washington Group Inc. stock. Washington Group is a Winston-Salem-based textile, convenience-store and ice-cream conglomerate that Bagley and James R. Gilley created in the early 1970s. Bagley, the 44-year-old grandson of R.J. Reynolds, is not a plaintiff in the suit. The article in question in The Star indicated that both Bagley and-his wife had been careless in their business and financial affairs. The lawsuit, filed in Superior Court for the District of Columbia, alleges libel, invasion of privacy and false light in the public eye. (AP) — Rogers C.B. Morton, cabinet secretary for two presidents, a fiveterm Maryland congressman and former head of the Republican Party, died at his home near here Thursday. He was 64. Morton, who was operated on for cancer of the prostate in 1973 and for a related problem in 1978, had been confined to his home for four weeks. The funeral will be Saturday at Christ Episcopal Church here. Morton served in Congress with two presidents-to-be — Richard Nixon and Gerald Ford — then in both their cabinets: interior secretary for Nixon, commerce secretary for Ford. Morton also served as a campaign official for both Nixon and Ford. Nixon had telephoned Morton only Wednesday.
